      "content": "# Challenge LEI and vLEI Data  
The centralized challenge facility made available by the[Global Legal Entity Identifier Foundation (GLEIF)](https://www.gleif.org/en/about/this-is-gleif)extends the ability to trigger updates of [Legal Entity Identifier (LEI)](https://www.gleif.org/en/about-lei/introducing-the-legal-entity-identifier-lei)data to all interested parties. Specifically, it offers an easy and convenient means to trigger the verification and, where required, speedy update of LEI records including related reference data.  
The GLEIF Data Challenge Facility provides any user of LEI data with the opportunity to substantiate doubts regarding the referential integrity between LEI records, or the accuracy and completeness of the related reference data. It also allows the indication of possible duplicate entries or any lack of timely response to LEI related corporate actions.  
The GLEIF Data Challenge Facility supports challenging relationship information shown on LEI Search. By exploring the LEI Reference Data of a specific LEI record, the user is able to request a data change on the declared direct and ultimate parent relationships and exceptions.  
One LEI data record may be challenged at a time (as many fields as needed within that record may be challenged). Challenging several LEI data records requires the entry of one challenge per record.

Should the correctness of an LEI data record be called into question through the GLEIF challenge facility, it is the responsibility of the relevant LEI issuing organization to resolve the matter in dialog with the impacted legal entity. If required, and subject to further verification against an authoritative source, the LEI issuer will update the information related to an LEI record. The LEI issuer aims to resolve a challenge within ten business days.  
Similarly, challenges related to vLEIs are submitted via email to [info@gleif.org](https://www.gleif.org/en/lei-data/gleif-data-quality-management/challenge-lei-and-vlei-data/mailto:info@gleif.org) and forwarded to the respective vLEI issuer by email, who are expected to respond in the same way.

| Country of Formation | The country under whose laws the entity is incorporated or organised |
| Entity Category | Whether the entity is a general or branch entity, a fund, or a special purpose entity |

| LEI Issuer (LOU) | The GLEIF-accredited Local Operating Unit that issued and manages this LEI |
| Initial Registration Date | The date on which the LEI was first issued |
| Next Renewal Date | The date by which the LEI must be renewed to remain active |

query: Who is Leopoldo Alejandro Betancourt López? What are his corporate affiliations and any known risks or red flags associated with him?
answer:
## Who is Leopoldo Alejandro Betancourt López?

Leopoldo Alejandro Betancourt López is a 46-year-old Venezuelan businessman born in Caracas in February 1980 (some sources state 1980 generally). He is estimated to have a net worth of approximately $2.6 billion. He studied Economics and Business Administration at Suffolk University in Massachusetts, earning a double major, and also attended Oxford University.

Betancourt is a descendant of Hermógenes López, the former acting president of Venezuela between 1887 and 1888. His father was a pianist and physician named Leopoldo Betancourt, and his mother is Lilia López, a jewelry designer from Valencia.

## Corporate Affiliations

Betancourt has extensive corporate affiliations spanning multiple countries and industries:

### Primary Companies:

**Derwick Associates**: Betancourt is the founder, Chairman and CEO of this engineering, procurement and construction company, which he founded in 2003 and registered internationally in Barbados in 2009. The company secured 12 no-bid contracts with the Venezuelan government between 2009 and 2011 to build power plants during Venezuela's energy crisis, reportedly worth approximately $5 billion.

**O'Hara Administration**: An international investment group based in Spain where Betancourt serves as the principal shareholder and director. Through O'Hara, he led investments in multiple ventures.

**Hawkers (Saldum Ventures, S.L.)**: Betancourt is the majority owner and President of this Spanish sunglasses company. In 2016, he led a €50 million investment round in Hawkers and became its president in November 2016.

**North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP)**: A Barbados-registered company that Betancourt co-founded in April 2024 and took full control of in 2025. NABEP recently secured operational control of 17 Venezuelan oil fields with estimated reserves exceeding 65 billion barrels through a deal with the Trump administration.

**Pacific Exploration & Production Corporation**: Betancourt became the largest shareholder in May 2015, controlling 19.5% of shares (later increased to 19.95%), and was appointed director and member of the board by August 2015.

**BDK Financial Group**: Betancourt is a major shareholder. The group's flagship, Banque de Dakar, was inaugurated in Senegal in June 2015, aiming to expand financial inclusion across French-speaking Africa.

**Auro Travel**: An investment in this Spanish ride-sharing/vehicle-for-hire service company, which became Spain's largest fleet operator for rental vehicles.

### Luxembourg Entities:

According to the OCCRP OpenLux investigation in 2021, Betancourt controls at least four companies registered in Luxembourg:
- Latin America Ventures SARL (incorporated 2015 with $100,000 capital; assets exceeded $253 million by year-end 2015)
- Gainsboro Developments
- Ming International
- O'Hara Financial S.A.

### Family-Connected Companies:

Transparencia Venezuela identified 54 companies (as of November 2025) in which Betancourt figured as a director or shareholder across 16 countries between 2009 and 2018. In 11 of these firms, family members also appear as shareholders or directors, including:
- His mother: Lilia Cristina López de Guzmán de Frutos
- His brothers: Gonzalo Adolfo Hermógenes Guzmán de Frutos López and Domingo Xavier Guzmán de Frutos López
- His cousins: Pedro Trebbau López and Francisco Antonio Convit Guruceaga

### Other Ventures:

- **Moneyback**: Co-founded Mexico's leading VAT refund platform for international travelers
- **JobandTalent**: Investment in this digital staffing platform
- **Guanábana Real Estate S.L.**: Real estate company registered in Spain in 2010 (his mother figured in this company until 2020)

### Paradise Papers Connection:

Betancourt appears as Director of ZGR International Corporation in the Paradise Papers documents.

## Known Risks and Red Flags

Betancourt faces significant legal and reputational risks across multiple jurisdictions:

### "Bolichicos" Background:

Betancourt is identified as one of the "bolichicos" (Bolivarian boys) - young Venezuelan businessmen who amassed fortunes through lucrative government contracts during the Hugo Chávez era despite lacking proven experience. His company Derwick Associates obtained 12 no-bid contracts for power plant construction during Venezuela's 2009 energy crisis.

**Alleged Overcharging**: Transparencia Venezuela reported in 2018 that 11 projects awarded to Derwick should have cost $2.1 billion but were billed at approximately $5 billion, representing alleged government overcharges exceeding $2.9 billion (a 138% overpayment). The organization also reported that several projects were either not finished or carried out incorrectly, with used and defective turbines installed that failed to stop recurring blackouts.

### Active Criminal Investigations:

**Switzerland**: 
- Betancourt was arrested in London in November 2025 on a Swiss international arrest warrant for alleged money laundering offenses between October 2010 and January 2018
- Swiss authorities allege involvement in laundering over 3.3 billion euros (approximately $3.5 billion) diverted from PDVSA (Venezuela's state oil company)
- He was released on £2 million bail with restrictions to travel only by helicopter between two luxury UK residences
- In May 2026, Switzerland withdrew its UK extradition request, reportedly after intervention by Trump administration officials (including then-Attorney General Pam Bondi and Deputy Todd Blanche), but Swiss prosecutors confirmed the criminal investigation remains open and continuing
- In January 2026, Swiss authorities froze assets linked to Betancourt as part of a broader freeze targeting politically exposed persons associated with Nicolás Maduro

**Spain**:
- Betancourt was first arrested in London in September 2025 under a European Arrest Warrant issued by Spain for alleged money laundering
- Spanish authorities raided his properties, including Alamín Castle (a palatial estate in Toledo province reportedly worth £21 million) in August 2025 as part of Operation Bolívar, but Betancourt had already left Spain via Lisbon
- Spain's Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office filed a lawsuit in June 2025 against Betancourt, his cousin Pedro Trebbau, partner Francisco Convit, and three others for alleged money laundering and tax crimes
- The Spanish investigation alleges Betancourt bribed three PDVSA officials with $42 million to defraud $4.85 billion in currency operations
- The Spanish arrest warrant was later withdrawn and replaced by the Swiss warrant
- As of September 2026, the Spanish investigation remains active despite U.S. intervention

**United States**:
- In 2013, former U.S. ambassador to Venezuela Otto Reich filed a lawsuit against Betancourt and associates for allegedly "paying large sums to [Venezuelan] public officials in exchange for awarding them contracts" (dismissed five years later on jurisdictional grounds)
- Federal court records identify Betancourt as "Conspirator 2" in Operation Money Flight, a $1.2 billion money-laundering scheme related to PDVSA corruption
- U.S. investigators sought Swiss banking information involving Derwick Associates, Pedro Trebbau, and Betancourt as part of investigations into possible payments to Venezuelan officials
- Despite these investigations, Betancourt has never been formally charged in the United States
- The Washington Post reported that senior Trump administration officials intervened with Swiss prosecutors regarding the investigation into Betancourt
- The U.S. Prosecutor's Office asked the Department of Justice to arrest Betancourt if he entered U.S. territory, but instead the U.S. government shielded him as a business partner

**Andorra and Portugal**: Investigations have also been opened in these jurisdictions related to alleged corruption schemes involving PDVSA.

### PDVSA Corruption Allegations:

In 2022, then-Venezuelan Minister of Petroleum Tareck El Aissami (now imprisoned in the Pdvsa-Cripto case) publicly identified Betancourt as one of the recipients in a corruption scheme that compromised $4.85 billion from PDVSA. However, a Venezuelan tribunal closed the case with a dismissal (sobreseimiento) in 2015, and current interim President Delcy Rodríguez stated in 2026 that Betancourt "was dismissed years ago" and has no pending cases in Venezuela.

### Rudy Giuliani Connection:

The Washington Post revealed that Rudy Giuliani defended Betancourt and pressured U.S. authorities not to file charges against him for money laundering and extortion in the United States.

### Luxembourg Offshore Structure Red Flags:

The OCCRP investigation highlighted that Latin America Ventures SARL, capitalized at only $100,000, held assets exceeding $253 million by 2015. This severe disparity between initial capital and actual assets is described as "a classic red flag for money laundering," indicating these shell companies may have been used to warehouse wealth acquired through allegedly corrupt means.

### Asset Freeze:

In January 2026, Switzerland froze assets belonging to Betancourt as part of a list of "politically exposed persons abroad and their associates" connected to Nicolás Maduro. Betancourt was linked to Latin America Ventures SARL, which filed a 2024 balance sheet showing assets of just $6.47 million, down from $252 million in its 2022 balance sheet.

### Family Members Under Investigation:

Two of Betancourt's cousins and former business partners, Francisco Convit and Pedro Trebbau, are also on the Swiss frozen assets list and named in various investigations. They are identified as associates of former Venezuelan vice minister of electric power Nervis Gerardo Villalobos Cárdenas, who is also under investigation.

### Current Legal Status:

- Betancourt has never been formally charged or convicted of any crime in any jurisdiction
- He was arrested twice in the UK in 2025 (September and November) but released on bail
- As of May 2026, UK travel restrictions were lifted after Switzerland withdrew its extradition request
- A five-day extradition hearing was scheduled for May 2025 in Westminster Magistrates Court
- His attorney, Thomas Clare, characterizes the allegations as "politically motivated" and states that any suggestion of corrupt activities is "categorically false"
- Sara Chouraqui, former head of the fraud and corruption division at the UK's Serious Fraud Office and now general counsel at NABEP, defends Betancourt as having "never been accused of any crime in any jurisdiction"

### Compliance and Due Diligence Concerns:

Multiple investigative journalism organizations, including the Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project (OCCRP), Transparencia Venezuela, and various media outlets, have documented alleged ties to corruption networks, money laundering, and embezzlement schemes. Anti-corruption expert Alejandro Rebolledo described Luxembourg as "an ideal place for people like Convit and Betancourt to hide illicit cash."

### Controversial Trump Administration Partnership:

Despite the ongoing investigations, Betancourt's company NABEP secured a major oil deal with the Trump administration in August 2026, granting operational control over 17 Venezuelan oil fields. This partnership has been described by critics as controversial, with Venezuelan-born human rights activist Thor Halvorssen calling Betancourt "a POS (piece of sh*t) that comes along only once per generation." The deal has raised questions about the Trump administration's priorities, with some observers suggesting it demonstrates that "predation and access to Venezuela's energy resources are Donald Trump's priority, rather than promoting a democratic transition."

### Summary of Risk Profile:

Betancourt presents significant compliance, reputational, and legal risks due to:
1. Active money laundering investigations in multiple jurisdictions (Switzerland, Spain)
2. Alleged involvement in multi-billion dollar corruption schemes related to Venezuelan state oil company PDVSA
3. Identification as "Conspirator 2" in U.S. federal investigation
4. Use of complex offshore structures in Luxembourg and other jurisdictions
5. Asset freezes by Swiss authorities
6. Allegations of no-bid contracts and massive overcharging during Venezuelan government projects
7. Association with other individuals under investigation or convicted of corruption
8. Classification as a "politically exposed person" by Swiss authorities
9. Extensive network of companies across multiple jurisdictions that may facilitate opacity

Despite these red flags, Betancourt maintains he has operated legally and has successfully avoided formal charges or convictions in any jurisdiction.

      "content": "# Alejandro Betancourt no es primo de Leopoldo López como corre por redes  \nA raíz de la participación de Alejandro Betancourt en el acuerdo petrolero recientemente anunciado entre Venezuela y Estados Unidos, y tras el repost de un video de Jorge Rodríguez grabado en 2019, una **falsa matriz de información** ha regresado nuevamente a las redes: Alejandro Betancourt y Leopoldo López son primos.  \nLa supuesta vinculación filial fue desmentida en 2022 por el portal de Verificación [EsPaja.com](https://espaja.com/fact-checking/alejandro-betancourt-es-familia-de-leopoldo-lopez) de la Organización Transparencia Venezuela. ## Who is Leopoldo Alejandro Betancourt López?

Leopoldo Alejandro Betancourt López is a 46-year-old Venezuelan businessman born in Caracas in February 1980 (some sources state 1980 generally). He is estimated to have a net worth of approximately $2.6 billion. He studied Economics and Business Administration at Suffolk University in Massachusetts, earning a double major, and also attended Oxford University.

Betancourt is a descendant of Hermógenes López, the former acting president of Venezuela between 1887 and 1888. His father was a pianist and physician named Leopoldo Betancourt, and his mother is Lilia López, a jewelry designer from Valencia.

## Corporate Affiliations

Betancourt has extensive corporate affiliations spanning multiple countries and industries:

### Primary Companies:

**Derwick Associates**: Betancourt is the founder, Chairman and CEO of this engineering, procurement and construction company, which he founded in 2003 and registered internationally in Barbados in 2009. The company secured 12 no-bid contracts with the Venezuelan government between 2009 and 2011 to build power plants during Venezuela's energy crisis, reportedly worth approximately $5 billion.

**O'Hara Administration**: An international investment group based in Spain where Betancourt serves as the principal shareholder and director. Through O'Hara, he led investments in multiple ventures.

**Hawkers (Saldum Ventures, S.L.)**: Betancourt is the majority owner and President of this Spanish sunglasses company. In 2016, he led a €50 million investment round in Hawkers and became its president in November 2016.

**North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP)**: A Barbados-registered company that Betancourt co-founded in April 2024 and took full control of in 2025. NABEP recently secured operational control of 17 Venezuelan oil fields with estimated reserves exceeding 65 billion barrels through a deal with the Trump administration.

**Pacific Exploration & Production Corporation**: Betancourt became the largest shareholder in May 2015, controlling 19.5% of shares (later increased to 19.95%), and was appointed director and member of the board by August 2015.

**BDK Financial Group**: Betancourt is a major shareholder. The group's flagship, Banque de Dakar, was inaugurated in Senegal in June 2015, aiming to expand financial inclusion across French-speaking Africa.

**Auro Travel**: An investment in this Spanish ride-sharing/vehicle-for-hire service company, which became Spain's largest fleet operator for rental vehicles.

### Luxembourg Entities:

According to the OCCRP OpenLux investigation in 2021, Betancourt controls at least four companies registered in Luxembourg:
- Latin America Ventures SARL (incorporated 2015 with $100,000 capital; assets exceeded $253 million by year-end 2015)
- Gainsboro Developments
- Ming International
- O'Hara Financial S.A.

### Family-Connected Companies:

Transparencia Venezuela identified 54 companies (as of November 2025) in which Betancourt figured as a director or shareholder across 16 countries between 2009 and 2018. In 11 of these firms, family members also appear as shareholders or directors, including:
- His mother: Lilia Cristina López de Guzmán de Frutos
- His brothers: Gonzalo Adolfo Hermógenes Guzmán de Frutos López and Domingo Xavier Guzmán de Frutos López
- His cousins: Pedro Trebbau López and Francisco Antonio Convit Guruceaga

### Other Ventures:

- **Moneyback**: Co-founded Mexico's leading VAT refund platform for international travelers
- **JobandTalent**: Investment in this digital staffing platform
- **Guanábana Real Estate S.L.**: Real estate company registered in Spain in 2010 (his mother figured in this company until 2020)

### Paradise Papers Connection:

Betancourt appears as Director of ZGR International Corporation in the Paradise Papers documents.

## Known Risks and Red Flags

Betancourt faces significant legal and reputational risks across multiple jurisdictions:

### "Bolichicos" Background:

Betancourt is identified as one of the "bolichicos" (Bolivarian boys) - young Venezuelan businessmen who amassed fortunes through lucrative government contracts during the Hugo Chávez era despite lacking proven experience. His company Derwick Associates obtained 12 no-bid contracts for power plant construction during Venezuela's 2009 energy crisis.

**Alleged Overcharging**: Transparencia Venezuela reported in 2018 that 11 projects awarded to Derwick should have cost $2.1 billion but were billed at approximately $5 billion, representing alleged government overcharges exceeding $2.9 billion (a 138% overpayment). The organization also reported that several projects were either not finished or carried out incorrectly, with used and defective turbines installed that failed to stop recurring blackouts.

### Active Criminal Investigations:

**Switzerland**: 
- Betancourt was arrested in London in November 2025 on a Swiss international arrest warrant for alleged money laundering offenses between October 2010 and January 2018
- Swiss authorities allege involvement in laundering over 3.3 billion euros (approximately $3.5 billion) diverted from PDVSA (Venezuela's state oil company)
- He was released on £2 million bail with restrictions to travel only by helicopter between two luxury UK residences
- In May 2026, Switzerland withdrew its UK extradition request, reportedly after intervention by Trump administration officials (including then-Attorney General Pam Bondi and Deputy Todd Blanche), but Swiss prosecutors confirmed the criminal investigation remains open and continuing
- In January 2026, Swiss authorities froze assets linked to Betancourt as part of a broader freeze targeting politically exposed persons associated with Nicolás Maduro

**Spain**:
- Betancourt was first arrested in London in September 2025 under a European Arrest Warrant issued by Spain for alleged money laundering
- Spanish authorities raided his properties, including Alamín Castle (a palatial estate in Toledo province reportedly worth £21 million) in August 2025 as part of Operation Bolívar, but Betancourt had already left Spain via Lisbon
- Spain's Anti-Corruption Prosecutor's Office filed a lawsuit in June 2025 against Betancourt, his cousin Pedro Trebbau, partner Francisco Convit, and three others for alleged money laundering and tax crimes
- The Spanish investigation alleges Betancourt bribed three PDVSA officials with $42 million to defraud $4.85 billion in currency operations
- The Spanish arrest warrant was later withdrawn and replaced by the Swiss warrant
- As of September 2026, the Spanish investigation remains active despite U.S. intervention

**United States**:
- In 2013, former U.S. ambassador to Venezuela Otto Reich filed a lawsuit against Betancourt and associates for allegedly "paying large sums to [Venezuelan] public officials in exchange for awarding them contracts" (dismissed five years later on jurisdictional grounds)
- Federal court records identify Betancourt as "Conspirator 2" in Operation Money Flight, a $1.2 billion money-laundering scheme related to PDVSA corruption
- U.S. investigators sought Swiss banking information involving Derwick Associates, Pedro Trebbau, and Betancourt as part of investigations into possible payments to Venezuelan officials
- Despite these investigations, Betancourt has never been formally charged in the United States
- The Washington Post reported that senior Trump administration officials intervened with Swiss prosecutors regarding the investigation into Betancourt
- The U.S. Prosecutor's Office asked the Department of Justice to arrest Betancourt if he entered U.S. territory, but instead the U.S. government shielded him as a business partner

**Andorra and Portugal**: Investigations have also been opened in these jurisdictions related to alleged corruption schemes involving PDVSA.

### PDVSA Corruption Allegations:

In 2022, then-Venezuelan Minister of Petroleum Tareck El Aissami (now imprisoned in the Pdvsa-Cripto case) publicly identified Betancourt as one of the recipients in a corruption scheme that compromised $4.85 billion from PDVSA. However, a Venezuelan tribunal closed the case with a dismissal (sobreseimiento) in 2015, and current interim President Delcy Rodríguez stated in 2026 that Betancourt "was dismissed years ago" and has no pending cases in Venezuela.

### Rudy Giuliani Connection:

The Washington Post revealed that Rudy Giuliani defended Betancourt and pressured U.S. authorities not to file charges against him for money laundering and extortion in the United States.

### Luxembourg Offshore Structure Red Flags:

The OCCRP investigation highlighted that Latin America Ventures SARL, capitalized at only $100,000, held assets exceeding $253 million by 2015. This severe disparity between initial capital and actual assets is described as "a classic red flag for money laundering," indicating these shell companies may have been used to warehouse wealth acquired through allegedly corrupt means.

### Asset Freeze:

In January 2026, Switzerland froze assets belonging to Betancourt as part of a list of "politically exposed persons abroad and their associates" connected to Nicolás Maduro. Betancourt was linked to Latin America Ventures SARL, which filed a 2024 balance sheet showing assets of just $6.47 million, down from $252 million in its 2022 balance sheet.

### Family Members Under Investigation:

Two of Betancourt's cousins and former business partners, Francisco Convit and Pedro Trebbau, are also on the Swiss frozen assets list and named in various investigations. They are identified as associates of former Venezuelan vice minister of electric power Nervis Gerardo Villalobos Cárdenas, who is also under investigation.

### Current Legal Status:

- Betancourt has never been formally charged or convicted of any crime in any jurisdiction
- He was arrested twice in the UK in 2025 (September and November) but released on bail
- As of May 2026, UK travel restrictions were lifted after Switzerland withdrew its extradition request
- A five-day extradition hearing was scheduled for May 2025 in Westminster Magistrates Court
- His attorney, Thomas Clare, characterizes the allegations as "politically motivated" and states that any suggestion of corrupt activities is "categorically false"
- Sara Chouraqui, former head of the fraud and corruption division at the UK's Serious Fraud Office and now general counsel at NABEP, defends Betancourt as having "never been accused of any crime in any jurisdiction"

### Compliance and Due Diligence Concerns:

Multiple investigative journalism organizations, including the Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project (OCCRP), Transparencia Venezuela, and various media outlets, have documented alleged ties to corruption networks, money laundering, and embezzlement schemes. Anti-corruption expert Alejandro Rebolledo described Luxembourg as "an ideal place for people like Convit and Betancourt to hide illicit cash."

### Controversial Trump Administration Partnership:

Despite the ongoing investigations, Betancourt's company NABEP secured a major oil deal with the Trump administration in August 2026, granting operational control over 17 Venezuelan oil fields. This partnership has been described by critics as controversial, with Venezuelan-born human rights activist Thor Halvorssen calling Betancourt "a POS (piece of sh*t) that comes along only once per generation." The deal has raised questions about the Trump administration's priorities, with some observers suggesting it demonstrates that "predation and access to Venezuela's energy resources are Donald Trump's priority, rather than promoting a democratic transition."

### Summary of Risk Profile:

1. Active money laundering investigations in multiple jurisdictions (Switzerland, Spain)

query: Who owns and controls Allwyn Investments Cyprus Ltd, and what companies is it connected to?
answer:
Based on the search results, here is what is known about Allwyn Investments Cyprus Ltd (formerly Rubidium Holding 2 Ltd):

## Ownership and Control

**Ultimate Ownership:**
Allwyn Investments Cyprus Ltd is a wholly-owned indirect subsidiary of Allwyn International AG (formerly SAZKA Group a.s.). The ultimate control structure is as follows:

- **KKCG Group AG** (controlled by Karel Komárek through the Valea Foundation) owns 95.73% of Allwyn International AG
- **J&T ARCH INVESTMENTS** owns 4.27% of Allwyn International AG (acquired in August 2025 for €500 million)
- Allwyn International AG owns Allwyn Investments Cyprus Ltd through its holding structure

**Key Control Person:**
Karel Komárek is the founder and chairman of KKCG Group AG and serves as the ultimate beneficial owner and controller of the Allwyn group, including Allwyn Investments Cyprus Ltd. He is a Czech billionaire entrepreneur worth approximately $9.4 billion as of March 2024.

## Corporate Structure and Name Changes

Allwyn Investments Cyprus Ltd underwent a rebranding in October 2022 as part of the Allwyn group's global rebranding initiative:
- **Former name:** Rubidium Holding 2 Ltd
- **Current name:** Allwyn Investment Cyprus Ltd (also referred to as Allwyn Investments Cyprus Limited)

The company is focused on the Cypriot market and is part of Allwyn's Greece & Cyprus regional sub-holding structure.

## Connected Companies

Allwyn Investments Cyprus Ltd is connected to numerous companies within the Allwyn group structure:

**Regional Holding Companies:**
- Allwyn Greece & Cyprus Holding Ltd (formerly SAZKA DELTA HELLENIC HOLDINGS LIMITED)
- Allwyn Greece & Cyprus Holding 2 Ltd (formerly Rubidium Holdings Limited)

**Parent Company:**
- Allwyn International AG (formerly SAZKA Group a.s.)
- Allwyn AG (formerly SAZKA Entertainment AG) - KKCG's wholly-owned subsidiary that holds the stake in Allwyn International AG

**Key Operating Companies in Greece & Cyprus:**
- OPAP S.A. (Greece and Cyprus) - Allwyn owned 51.78% of OPAP as of the merger announcement in October 2025, with a business combination completed in March 2026 creating the second-largest listed lottery and gaming operator globally
- Allwyn Hellas (formerly OPAP S.A., renamed Allwyn AG after the March 2026 merger completion)
- Stoiximan - online sports betting and iGaming operator in Greece and Cyprus (100% owned by OPAP/Allwyn as of August 2025)

**Other Regional Operating Companies:**
- Camelot UK (United Kingdom)
- Camelot Lottery Solutions (United States - Illinois)
- Casinos Austria (Austria)
- SAZKA (Czech Republic)
- LottoItalia (Italy) - 32.5% minority stake

**Investment Holdings:**
- Kaizen Gaming Limited (Betano) - Allwyn Investments Cyprus Ltd acquired a 36.75% minority interest in Betano's operations outside Greece and Cyprus from OPAP Investment Limited in December 2022 for €74.243 million. This transaction involved a share purchase agreement where OPAP Investment Limited (a 100% subsidiary of OPAP) transferred the stake to Allwyn Investments Cyprus Ltd.

**Other Group Companies:**
- MND Group (energy)
- ARICOMA Group (IT)
- KKCG Real Estate Group
- Instant Win Gaming (e-instants supplier)
- Novibet (51% stake acquired in December 2024)
- PrizePicks (62.3% majority stake acquired in January 2026)

**Controlling Shareholder:**
- KKCG Group AG - the investment and innovation group founded by Karel Komárek, operating in 37 countries with over 16,000 employees and more than €10 billion in assets under management

The ownership structure, holding structure, and activities of Allwyn Investments Cyprus Ltd have remained the same despite the name change, with only the legal name being modified to align with the Allwyn brand.

      "content": "# Cyprus Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) Law: What International Investors need to Know  
Cyprus has recently implemented its Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) screening regime, introducing for the first time a formal framework for the review of foreign investments connected to strategic sectors in Cyprus. The regime aligns Cyprus with the broader European regulatory framework under Regulation (EU) 2019/452 and reflects the increasing focus across the EU on the protection of security, public order, critical infrastructure and sensitive technologies, while reinforcing Cyprus’ position as an established international investment and business hub.  
The new framework is expected to have a significant impact on international investors, private equity and venture capital funds, multinational groups, technology companies and cross-border transactions involving businesses operating in strategic sectors connected with Cyprus.  
Given the broad scope of the legislation, early assessment of potential filing obligations has become an important component of transaction planning for foreign investors and their advisors.
## Practical Implications for Investors and Businesses  
The Cyprus FDI framework introduces an additional regulatory layer for cross-border transactions involving strategic sectors connected to Cyprus.  
Particular attention should now be given to:  
- ownership and control structures;
- ultimate beneficial ownership arrangements;
- investments involving technology, AI, data or critical infrastructure;
- transaction timelines and conditionality; and
- regulatory risk allocation within transaction documents.  
The legislation is expected to be particularly relevant for:  
- private equity and venture capital transactions;
- technology and AI businesses;
- fintech and digital infrastructure companies;
- healthcare and biotech transactions; and
- multinational groups using Cyprus as part of broader international structures.
## Conclusion  
The Cyprus FDI Law establishes a broad foreign investment screening mechanism consistent with the wider European regulatory trend towards increased scrutiny of foreign investments in sensitive sectors.  
Given the potentially extensive scope of the legislation and the significant penalties for non-compliance, foreign investors and transaction parties should assess potential filing obligations at an early stage of any transaction involving Cyprus-connected strategic activities.

Based on the search results, here is what is known about Allwyn Investments Cyprus Ltd (formerly Rubidium Holding 2 Ltd):

## Ownership and Control

**Ultimate Ownership:**
Allwyn Investments Cyprus Ltd is a wholly-owned indirect subsidiary of Allwyn International AG (formerly SAZKA Group a.s.). The ultimate control structure is as follows:

- **KKCG Group AG** (controlled by Karel Komárek through the Valea Foundation) owns 95.73% of Allwyn International AG
- **J&T ARCH INVESTMENTS** owns 4.27% of Allwyn International AG (acquired in August 2025 for €500 million)
- Allwyn International AG owns Allwyn Investments Cyprus Ltd through its holding structure

**Key Control Person:**
Karel Komárek is the founder and chairman of KKCG Group AG and serves as the ultimate beneficial owner and controller of the Allwyn group, including Allwyn Investments Cyprus Ltd. He is a Czech billionaire entrepreneur worth approximately $9.4 billion as of March 2024.

## Corporate Structure and Name Changes

Allwyn Investments Cyprus Ltd underwent a rebranding in October 2022 as part of the Allwyn group's global rebranding initiative:
- **Former name:** Rubidium Holding 2 Ltd
- **Current name:** Allwyn Investment Cyprus Ltd (also referred to as Allwyn Investments Cyprus Limited)

The company is focused on the Cypriot market and is part of Allwyn's Greece & Cyprus regional sub-holding structure.

## Connected Companies

Allwyn Investments Cyprus Ltd is connected to numerous companies within the Allwyn group structure:

**Regional Holding Companies:**
- Allwyn Greece & Cyprus Holding Ltd (formerly SAZKA DELTA HELLENIC HOLDINGS LIMITED)
- Allwyn Greece & Cyprus Holding 2 Ltd (formerly Rubidium Holdings Limited)

**Parent Company:**
- Allwyn International AG (formerly SAZKA Group a.s.)
- Allwyn AG (formerly SAZKA Entertainment AG) - KKCG's wholly-owned subsidiary that holds the stake in Allwyn International AG

**Key Operating Companies in Greece & Cyprus:**
- OPAP S.A. (Greece and Cyprus) - Allwyn owned 51.78% of OPAP as of the merger announcement in October 2025, with a business combination completed in March 2026 creating the second-largest listed lottery and gaming operator globally
- Allwyn Hellas (formerly OPAP S.A., renamed Allwyn AG after the March 2026 merger completion)
- Stoiximan - online sports betting and iGaming operator in Greece and Cyprus (100% owned by OPAP/Allwyn as of August 2025)

**Other Regional Operating Companies:**
- Camelot UK (United Kingdom)
- Camelot Lottery Solutions (United States - Illinois)
- Casinos Austria (Austria)
- SAZKA (Czech Republic)
- LottoItalia (Italy) - 32.5% minority stake

**Investment Holdings:**
- Kaizen Gaming Limited (Betano) - Allwyn Investments Cyprus Ltd acquired a 36.75% minority interest in Betano's operations outside Greece and Cyprus from OPAP Investment Limited in December 2022 for €74.243 million. This transaction involved a share purchase agreement where OPAP Investment Limited (a 100% subsidiary of OPAP) transferred the stake to Allwyn Investments Cyprus Ltd.

**Other Group Companies:**
- MND Group (energy)
- ARICOMA Group (IT)
- KKCG Real Estate Group
- Instant Win Gaming (e-instants supplier)
- Novibet (51% stake acquired in December 2024)
- PrizePicks (62.3% majority stake acquired in January 2026)

**Controlling Shareholder:**
- KKCG Group AG - the investment and innovation group founded by Karel Komárek, operating in 37 countries with over 16,000 employees and more than €10 billion in assets under management

The ownership structure, holding structure, and activities of Allwyn Investments Cyprus Ltd have remained the same despite the name change, with only the legal name being modified to align with the Allwyn brand.

answer:
Ali Ansari is a Dubai-based Iranian banker and businessman who has been designated under multiple international sanctions regimes for his alleged role in financing Iran's leadership and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

## Identity and Background

Ali Ansari (also known as Ali Aliakbar Ansari) was born in December 1962 in southern Mehrabad, Tehran, and is originally from Ghazvin. He was the founder, owner, and director of Ayandeh Bank, which was established in 2013 through the merger of TAT Bank (which Ansari founded in 2009), Salehin Credit Institution, and ATI Credit Institution. Ayandeh Bank collapsed and was dissolved by Iranian authorities in mid-October 2025, with the Central Bank of Iran forcing its merger into Bank Melli Iran. The bank had approximately 7.6 million depositors and operated 270 branches across Iran, including 150 in Tehran.

## Sanctions and Watchlist Designations

Ali Ansari is subject to sanctions from multiple jurisdictions:

### United Kingdom Sanctions
- **Date**: October 30, 2025
- **Authority**: UK Government under Iran Sanctions Regulations (2023)
- **Measures**: Asset freeze, director disqualification, and travel ban
- **Reason**: Sanctioned for his role in financially enabling the work of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). The UK described him as a "corrupt Iranian banker and businessman" who funded "hostile activity" by Iran's elite Revolutionary Guards force.
- **Assets Frozen**: London property portfolio worth more than £150 million, including 12 mansions on The Bishops Avenue (nicknamed "Billionaires' Row") purchased for £73 million, another mansion on the same street for £33.7 million, and luxury flats near Kensington Palace.

### United States Sanctions
- **Date**: July 10, 2026
- **Authority**: U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC)
- **Executive Orders**: Designated pursuant to E.O. 13876 (for materially assisting Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei) and E.O. 13224, as amended (for acting on behalf of the IRGC)
- **Measures**: Asset freeze and prohibition on U.S. persons conducting transactions with him
- **Reason**: OFAC accused Ansari of being a "key financier" for Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei and other regime elites, alleging he "institutionalized embezzlement within the Iranian regime" and diverted publicly funded wealth into overseas real estate and commercial holdings.

### European Union Sanctions
- **Date**: July 30, 2026
- **Authority**: EU Council under Regulation (EU) 267/2012
- **Reason**: The EU stated that Ansari uses foreign banking channels to transfer funds abroad derived from Iranian oil sales, and acquires substantial assets including real estate in the EU and UK on behalf of persons connected to the Iranian leadership, including Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, thereby providing support to the Government of Iran.

### Other Listings
- Ansari appears on the French National Asset Freezing System
- Listed on the U.S. Consolidated Screening List (CSL)
- Listed on OpenSanctions and other sanctions databases

**Note**: Ansari holds multiple passports, including from Iran, Cyprus, and Saint Kitts and Nevis, according to UK sanctions filings.

Ali Ansari is connected to an extensive network of companies spanning multiple jurisdictions, valued at approximately €400 million in European real estate holdings:

### Primary Holding Company
**Smart Global Limited** (formerly Ziba Leisure Limited)
- Jurisdiction: Saint Kitts and Nevis
- Established: 2011
- Status: Sanctioned by OFAC on July 10, 2026
- Role: Central holding company through which Ansari invested in real estate and commercial properties throughout Germany, Luxembourg, Spain, the United Kingdom, Cyprus, the United Arab Emirates, and beyond
- UK corporate filings identify Ansari as the ultimate beneficial owner

### Banking Entities

**Ayandeh Bank** (defunct)
- Founded: 2013 (through merger)
- Status: Bankrupt and dissolved in October 2025; merged into Bank Melli Iran
- Role: Ansari was the principal shareholder (controlling approximately 65% through affiliated entities), owner, and director
- Issues: Accused of running a Ponzi scheme, extending more than 140 trillion tomans in loans to affiliated entities (mostly classified as doubtful receivables), with the largest borrower being Iran Mall International Development Company (accounting for roughly 70% of related-party loans)
- Subsidiaries:
  - Sanjesh Omid Ayandeh (investment consulting and financial services)
  - Ertebat Farda (electronic commerce company)
  - Ayandeh Bank Brokerage Company

**TAT Bank** (predecessor to Ayandeh Bank)
- Founded: 2009 by Ali Ansari
- Status: Merged into Ayandeh Bank in 2013
- Issues: Under investigation for widespread financial irregularities within three years of founding

### Luxembourg Companies

### Isle of Man Company

**Birch Ventures Limited**
- Jurisdiction: Isle of Man
- Role: Subsidiary of Smart Global Limited used to purchase London properties
- Assets: Portfolio of 12 derelict mansions on The Bishops Avenue, London (£73 million) and another mansion on the same street (£33.7 million)

### Real Estate Holdings and Operating Companies

The corporate structure extends to operating companies holding the following properties:

**Spain:**
- Steigenberger Golf & Spa Resort, Camp de Mar, Mallorca (164-room luxury hotel)
- Estimated value: €22 million

**Germany:**
- Hilton Frankfurt City Centre
- Hilton Frankfurt Gravenbruch
- Combined estimated value: €80 million
- Bero Oberhausen Shopping Centre (northwestern Germany)
- Estimated value: €68 million

**Austria:**
- Schlosshotel Kitzbühel (luxury ski resort in the Austrian Alps)

**United Kingdom:**
- 12 mansions on The Bishops Avenue, London (£73 million)
- Additional mansion on The Bishops Avenue (£33.7 million)
- Luxury flats near Kensington Palace
- 11 luxury mansions on Bishops Avenue in north London (according to some reports)
- Total UK frozen assets: Over £150 million

### Investment and Development Companies

**TAT Investing Co.** (Head of Ayandeh Bank)
- Type: Multinational investing company
- Described as the largest private investing company in the Middle East
- Portfolio includes:
  - Ayandeh Bank (largest private bank in Iran)
  - Iran Mall (largest mall in the world)
  - Furniture Malls (1, 2, 3)
  - Razi Insurance Co.
  - Farmanieh Mall
  - Mashhad Mall
  - Iran's Mobile Mall
  - Several towers and hotels
  - Digital subsidiaries
  - Several factories

**Iran Mall International Development Company**
- Role: Largest borrower from Ayandeh Bank
- Debt: Accounted for roughly 70% of all related-party loans from Ayandeh Bank
- Asset: Iran Mall (opened 2018, twice the size of the Pentagon)
- Attempted sale: December 2020 announcement to sell for $3.5 billion
- Auction attempt: December 2020 auction of Iran Mall shares for 34 trillion rials ($32 million) yielded no results

### Currency Exchange Houses (also sanctioned)

OFAC also sanctioned three Iran-based currency exchange houses along with Ansari:
- **Mohammad Darbani and Partners**
- **Lavasani and Partners General Partnership Company** (held hundreds of millions of dollars in foreign currency for sanctioned Iranian banks as of early 2026; contracts with Bank Melli, Bank Saderat, Sina Bank, Shahr Bank, Eghtesad Novin Bank, Tourism Bank, Bank Pasargad, and Bank Mellat)
- **Mohsen Khandan and Partners**

### Front Companies

OFAC also designated front companies used by Iranian exchange houses:
- **CDM Trading Limited** (Hong Kong-based)
- **Naba Alzaki Raw Materials Trading LLC** (UAE-based)

## Allegations and Legal Position

U.S. authorities allege that Ansari:
- Used his position at Ayandeh Bank to overextend loans and embezzle billions of dollars from the Iranian people
- Accumulated millions of dollars in holdings through shell companies and bank accounts across multiple jurisdictions
- Invested "the Iranian people's money" into real estate and commercial properties on behalf of Mojtaba Khamenei and other regime insiders
- Contributed to approximately 25% of total liquidity expansion and roughly 7% of national inflation in Iran over two decades

**Ansari's Response**: Through his lawyer Roger Gherson, Ansari has strongly denied any financial relationship with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps or the Supreme Leader, and stated his intention to challenge the UK government's sanctions decision. After Ayandeh Bank's failure, Ansari blamed the collapse on "decisions and policies beyond his control."

## Current Status

- Ansari is not currently on the European Union's sanctions list (as of the search date), though the EU added him to its Iran sanctions list in July 2026
- Luxembourg is not obliged to freeze Ansari's assets under EU law since enforcement is based on UN and EU sanctions
- OFAC issued Iran General License Y to allow a narrow, supervised wind-down of Smart Global Limited transactions
- The complex corporate structure spanning multiple jurisdictions continues to operate in areas where sanctions do not apply, highlighting gaps in international sanctions coordination

      "content": "A shocking revelation has emerged from Iran, where a major bank collapse has sent shockwaves through the country's economy and sparked widespread protests. This is a story of corruption, economic mismanagement, and the growing unrest among ordinary Iranians.  
**The Rise and Fall of Ayandeh Bank: A Ponzi Scheme Unveiled**  
Ayandeh Bank, once a beacon of promise, has crumbled, leaving behind a trail of economic devastation. With nearly $5 billion in losses and a mountain of bad loans, this bank, run by regime insiders, has become a symbol of the nation's economic woes.  
But here's where it gets controversial: Ayandeh Bank offered the highest interest rates in Iran, attracting millions of depositors. However, its success was built on a fragile foundation. The bank relied heavily on the government's printing of inflationary money, a practice that ultimately led to its downfall.  
And this is the part most people miss: Ayandeh Bank engaged in self-lending, lending money to many of the bank founder's own companies. It was a classic Ponzi scheme, as even the director of bank supervision at the Iranian central bank admitted last year.  
The bank's largest investment, the Iran Mall, is a testament to its excess. This opulent mall, twice the size of the Pentagon, opened its doors in 2018 amidst a spiraling currency crisis, falling wages, and skyrocketing food prices. It's a stark contrast to the struggles of ordinary Iranians.
As the economic crisis deepened, the Iranian government tried to cover up the bank's collapse by folding it into the country's largest state-owned lender, Bank Melli. But the damage was done. At least five other Iranian banks are on the brink of collapse, according to reports.  
The bank crisis coincided with a 12-day war with Israel and the US in June, further weakening Iran's position. Sanctions from the US and Europe directed oil revenue away from Iran, and the US clamped down on money laundering from Iraq.  
The value of the rial plummeted so rapidly that shop owners couldn't keep up with pricing, and importers lost money before they could even list their goods. This economic turmoil led to protests, with hundreds of merchants, usually apolitical, taking to the streets of Tehran.  
Despite an internet blackout and a government crackdown, thousands have demonstrated across Iran. According to estimates, more than 2,500 people have been killed during these protests.  
Days after Ayandeh Bank's collapse, the UK sanctioned the bank's founder, Ali Ansari, a wealthy Iranian businessman and an ally of former President Mahmoud Ahmadinejad. The UK labeled Ansari a "corrupt Iranian banker and businessman," accusing him of financing the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.  
Ansari, in a statement, blamed the bank's failure on decisions and policies beyond his control.

input.answer:
Ali Ansari is a Dubai-based Iranian banker and businessman who has been designated under multiple international sanctions regimes for his alleged role in financing Iran's leadership and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

## Identity and Background

Ali Ansari (also known as Ali Aliakbar Ansari) was born in December 1962 in southern Mehrabad, Tehran, and is originally from Ghazvin. He was the founder, owner, and director of Ayandeh Bank, which was established in 2013 through the merger of TAT Bank (which Ansari founded in 2009), Salehin Credit Institution, and ATI Credit Institution. Ayandeh Bank collapsed and was dissolved by Iranian authorities in mid-October 2025, with the Central Bank of Iran forcing its merger into Bank Melli Iran. The bank had approximately 7.6 million depositors and operated 270 branches across Iran, including 150 in Tehran.

## Sanctions and Watchlist Designations

Ali Ansari is subject to sanctions from multiple jurisdictions:

### United Kingdom Sanctions
- **Date**: October 30, 2025
- **Authority**: UK Government under Iran Sanctions Regulations (2023)
- **Measures**: Asset freeze, director disqualification, and travel ban
- **Reason**: Sanctioned for his role in financially enabling the work of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). The UK described him as a "corrupt Iranian banker and businessman" who funded "hostile activity" by Iran's elite Revolutionary Guards force.
- **Assets Frozen**: London property portfolio worth more than £150 million, including 12 mansions on The Bishops Avenue (nicknamed "Billionaires' Row") purchased for £73 million, another mansion on the same street for £33.7 million, and luxury flats near Kensington Palace.

### United States Sanctions
- **Date**: July 10, 2026
- **Authority**: U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC)
- **Executive Orders**: Designated pursuant to E.O. 13876 (for materially assisting Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei) and E.O. 13224, as amended (for acting on behalf of the IRGC)
- **Measures**: Asset freeze and prohibition on U.S. persons conducting transactions with him
- **Reason**: OFAC accused Ansari of being a "key financier" for Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei and other regime elites, alleging he "institutionalized embezzlement within the Iranian regime" and diverted publicly funded wealth into overseas real estate and commercial holdings.

### European Union Sanctions
- **Date**: July 30, 2026
- **Authority**: EU Council under Regulation (EU) 267/2012
- **Reason**: The EU stated that Ansari uses foreign banking channels to transfer funds abroad derived from Iranian oil sales, and acquires substantial assets including real estate in the EU and UK on behalf of persons connected to the Iranian leadership, including Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, thereby providing support to the Government of Iran.

### Other Listings
- Ansari appears on the French National Asset Freezing System
- Listed on the U.S. Consolidated Screening List (CSL)
- Listed on OpenSanctions and other sanctions databases

**Note**: Ansari holds multiple passports, including from Iran, Cyprus, and Saint Kitts and Nevis, according to UK sanctions filings.

## Companies and Business Connections

Ali Ansari is connected to an extensive network of companies spanning multiple jurisdictions, valued at approximately €400 million in European real estate holdings:

### Primary Holding Company
**Smart Global Limited** (formerly Ziba Leisure Limited)
- Jurisdiction: Saint Kitts and Nevis
- Established: 2011
- Status: Sanctioned by OFAC on July 10, 2026
- Role: Central holding company through which Ansari invested in real estate and commercial properties throughout Germany, Luxembourg, Spain, the United Kingdom, Cyprus, the United Arab Emirates, and beyond
- UK corporate filings identify Ansari as the ultimate beneficial owner

### Banking Entities

**Ayandeh Bank** (defunct)
- Founded: 2013 (through merger)
- Status: Bankrupt and dissolved in October 2025; merged into Bank Melli Iran
- Role: Ansari was the principal shareholder (controlling approximately 65% through affiliated entities), owner, and director
- Issues: Accused of running a Ponzi scheme, extending more than 140 trillion tomans in loans to affiliated entities (mostly classified as doubtful receivables), with the largest borrower being Iran Mall International Development Company (accounting for roughly 70% of related-party loans)
- Subsidiaries:
  - Sanjesh Omid Ayandeh (investment consulting and financial services)
  - Ertebat Farda (electronic commerce company)
  - Ayandeh Bank Brokerage Company

**TAT Bank** (predecessor to Ayandeh Bank)
- Founded: 2009 by Ali Ansari
- Status: Merged into Ayandeh Bank in 2013
- Issues: Under investigation for widespread financial irregularities within three years of founding

### Luxembourg Companies

**Tidalwave Holdings** (multiple entities)
- Tidalwave Holdings I S.à r.l. (Luxembourg)
- Tidalwave Holdings II S.à r.l. (Luxembourg) - RCS B193240
  - Incorporated: January 12, 2015
  - Registered address: 11, rue de l'Industrie, Windhof, Luxembourg
  - Shareholder: Smart Global Limited
  - Holds 94% stake in Tidalwave Corporation (Netherlands)

**Leopard Germany Bero 1 S.à r.l.** (Luxembourg)
- Purpose: Holding company for German shopping centre investment (Bero Oberhausen)
- Purchase price: €49 million according to Luxembourg filings

**Leopard Germany Bero 2 S.à r.l.** (Luxembourg) - RCS B161274

**Leopard Germany Bero Holding 1 S.à r.l.** (Luxembourg) - RCS B160736

### Isle of Man Company

**Birch Ventures Limited**
- Jurisdiction: Isle of Man
- Role: Subsidiary of Smart Global Limited used to purchase London properties
- Assets: Portfolio of 12 derelict mansions on The Bishops Avenue, London (£73 million) and another mansion on the same street (£33.7 million)

### Real Estate Holdings and Operating Companies

The corporate structure extends to operating companies holding the following properties:

**Spain:**
- Steigenberger Golf & Spa Resort, Camp de Mar, Mallorca (164-room luxury hotel)
- Estimated value: €22 million

**Germany:**
- Hilton Frankfurt City Centre
- Hilton Frankfurt Gravenbruch
- Combined estimated value: €80 million
- Bero Oberhausen Shopping Centre (northwestern Germany)
- Estimated value: €68 million

**Austria:**
- Schlosshotel Kitzbühel (luxury ski resort in the Austrian Alps)

**United Kingdom:**
- 12 mansions on The Bishops Avenue, London (£73 million)
- Additional mansion on The Bishops Avenue (£33.7 million)
- Luxury flats near Kensington Palace
- 11 luxury mansions on Bishops Avenue in north London (according to some reports)
- Total UK frozen assets: Over £150 million

### Investment and Development Companies

**TAT Investing Co.** (Head of Ayandeh Bank)
- Type: Multinational investing company
- Described as the largest private investing company in the Middle East
- Portfolio includes:
  - Ayandeh Bank (largest private bank in Iran)
  - Iran Mall (largest mall in the world)
  - Furniture Malls (1, 2, 3)
  - Razi Insurance Co.
  - Farmanieh Mall
  - Mashhad Mall
  - Iran's Mobile Mall
  - Several towers and hotels
  - Digital subsidiaries
  - Several factories

**Iran Mall International Development Company**
- Role: Largest borrower from Ayandeh Bank
- Debt: Accounted for roughly 70% of all related-party loans from Ayandeh Bank
- Asset: Iran Mall (opened 2018, twice the size of the Pentagon)
- Attempted sale: December 2020 announcement to sell for $3.5 billion
- Auction attempt: December 2020 auction of Iran Mall shares for 34 trillion rials ($32 million) yielded no results

### Currency Exchange Houses (also sanctioned)

OFAC also sanctioned three Iran-based currency exchange houses along with Ansari:
- **Mohammad Darbani and Partners**
- **Lavasani and Partners General Partnership Company** (held hundreds of millions of dollars in foreign currency for sanctioned Iranian banks as of early 2026; contracts with Bank Melli, Bank Saderat, Sina Bank, Shahr Bank, Eghtesad Novin Bank, Tourism Bank, Bank Pasargad, and Bank Mellat)
- **Mohsen Khandan and Partners**

### Front Companies

OFAC also designated front companies used by Iranian exchange houses:
- **CDM Trading Limited** (Hong Kong-based)
- **Naba Alzaki Raw Materials Trading LLC** (UAE-based)

## Allegations and Legal Position

U.S. authorities allege that Ansari:
- Used his position at Ayandeh Bank to overextend loans and embezzle billions of dollars from the Iranian people
- Accumulated millions of dollars in holdings through shell companies and bank accounts across multiple jurisdictions
- Invested "the Iranian people's money" into real estate and commercial properties on behalf of Mojtaba Khamenei and other regime insiders
- Contributed to approximately 25% of total liquidity expansion and roughly 7% of national inflation in Iran over two decades

**Ansari's Response**: Through his lawyer Roger Gherson, Ansari has strongly denied any financial relationship with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps or the Supreme Leader, and stated his intention to challenge the UK government's sanctions decision. After Ayandeh Bank's failure, Ansari blamed the collapse on "decisions and policies beyond his control."

## Current Status

- Ansari is not currently on the European Union's sanctions list (as of the search date), though the EU added him to its Iran sanctions list in July 2026
- Luxembourg is not obliged to freeze Ansari's assets under EU law since enforcement is based on UN and EU sanctions
- OFAC issued Iran General License Y to allow a narrow, supervised wind-down of Smart Global Limited transactions
- The complex corporate structure spanning multiple jurisdictions continues to operate in areas where sanctions do not apply, highlighting gaps in international sanctions coordination

Smart Global Limited, a Saint Kitts and Nevis holding company established in 2011 (formerly Ziba Leisure Limited), is the central vehicle through which Ansari invested in real estate across Germany, Luxembourg, Spain, the UK, Cyprus, and the UAE.
OFAC sanctioned Smart Global Limited on July 10, 2026, for being owned or controlled by Ali Ansari.

Ayandeh Bank was established in 2013 through the merger of TAT Bank, Salehin Credit Institution, and ATI Credit Institution, with Ansari as principal shareholder controlling approximately 65% through affiliated entities.
Ayandeh Bank collapsed in October 2025 and was merged into Bank Melli Iran by the Central Bank of Iran, with approximately 7.6 million depositors and 270 branches.
Ayandeh Bank extended more than 140 trillion tomans in loans to affiliated entities, with Iran Mall International Development Company accounting for roughly 70% of related-party loans.
Luxembourg companies in Ansari's network include Tidalwave Holdings I and II S.à r.l. and Leopard Germany Bero 1 S.à r.l.
Tidalwave Holdings II S.à r.l. was incorporated on January 12, 2015, and is registered at 11, rue de l'Industrie, Windhof, Luxembourg, with Smart Global Limited as shareholder.
Birch Ventures Limited, an Isle of Man company and subsidiary of Smart Global Limited, was used to purchase a £73 million portfolio of 12 mansions on London's The Bishops Avenue.

Ansari's European property portfolio, valued at approximately €400 million, includes the Steigenberger Golf & Spa Resort in Mallorca (€22 million), two Hilton hotels in Frankfurt (€80 million combined), the Bero Oberhausen Shopping Centre (€68 million), and the Schlosshotel Kitzbühel in Austria.

TAT Investing Co. is described as the largest private investing company in the Middle East, with a portfolio including Ayandeh Bank, Iran Mall, Razi Insurance Co., and several malls, towers, hotels, and factories.
Iran Mall, the largest mall in the world and twice the size of the Pentagon, opened in 2018 and was Ayandeh Bank's largest investment.

OFAC also sanctioned three Iran-based currency exchange houses: Mohammad Darbani and Partners, Lavasani and Partners, and Mohsen Khandan and Partners, along with front companies CDM Trading Limited (Hong Kong) and Naba Alzaki Raw Materials Trading LLC (UAE).
Ansari, through his lawyer Roger Gherson, strongly denies any financial relationship with the IRGC and intends to challenge the UK sanctions.
Ansari is not currently on the EU sanctions list as a binding obligation for Luxembourg, though the EU added him to its Iran sanctions list in July 2026.
